title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
gist: A team led by NASA JPL's Yang Liu reports in Science that Teghaza 001, a Martian meteorite found in Mali's Sahara in 2022, is a single intact igneous rock dated to at least 4.1 billion years, making it only the third known ancient Martian meteorite. Its chemistry indicates active water circulation through the early Martian crust and a deep, garnet-bearing mantle source unlike any other Martian meteorite, likely from the southern highlands northwest of Hellas basin.

insights.claim: Crater counts suggest most of Mars' surface is over 3 billion years old, yet the three main Martian meteorite classes (shergottites, nakhlites, chassignites) are all 2.4 billion years old or younger; before Teghaza 001 only Allan Hills 84001 and Black Beauty were genuinely ancient.
